newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude softer, Urals, West African hold stead.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude softer, Urals, West African hold stead.

text.p: The North Sea crude market looked soft on Thursday despite a lack of physical action, with a weaker Brent paper market encouraging bearish sentiment, traders said.
"I think the market is at least going to stay down at these sort of levels and perhaps go lower," one said.
More Forties were seen on offer after half a dozen cargoes moved on Wednesday at premiums to Dated Brent in the low 30s.
"I think the levels that were traded yesterday will become today's offer levels," said a trader for a European major.
Wet Brent has shed some 15 cents this week.
Two Jan 24-26 cargoes traded yesterday at Feb Brent -24 cents.
Differentials for other North Sea grades such as Oseberg and Statfjord have also softened, but traders said that production problems at Norway's Ekofisk field may help limit further falls.

Ekofisk operator Phillips said on Thursday that it expected to resume production at the 350,000 barrel per day field at the weekend after it was shut in early on Tuesday because of a gas leak in a pipeline.
No Brent dates were due to turn wet on Thursday. The first dates from the February programme will emerge on Friday.
On paper, Brent intermonth spreads slid with Feb/Mar traded at +33 and +35 cents. Mar/Apr fell to +42/+45 and Apr/May traded lower at +45 cents.
"In ten minutes the spreads just came right off," said one paper trader.
IPE Feb Brent was trading some 34 cents lower at 1327 GMT ahead of its expiry at the close of business today.
March Brent paper fared worse, sheding nearly 50 cents to trade around $23.15/$23.20 a barrel.
CFDs for next week also slipped back to trade at Feb -18 cents, with the following week talk at +11/+16 cents.
